walkthroughs.body_html:
Parallel lines have the same gradient. Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to −1.

If a line has gradient 2, a parallel line also has gradient 2. A perpendicular line has gradient −1/2 (or −0.5).

Trick: flip the fraction and swap the sign — the negative reciprocal.

The midpoint of (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is ((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2) — just average the coordinates.

Midpoint of (2, 3) and (8, 7): x = (2+8)/2 = 5, y = (3+7)/2 = 5.

Midpoint = (5, 5).

Use Pythagoras on the horizontal and vertical gaps.

Distance = √((x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²).

From (1, 2) to (4, 6): differences are 3 and 4. Distance = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5.
